myths.Agent_1:
In the beginning, the mountains were perfectly silent. They stood as ancient giants, watching the valleys below but never speaking, for they had no voices of their own. Among the valley dwellers lived a young girl named Aella, whose laughter was so joyous it made the spring flowers bloom.

One day, the North Wind grew jealous of Aella's radiant spirit and swept down to steal her voice. The wind snatched her laughter from her throat, carrying it far up into the craggy, desolate peaks. Heartbroken and silent, Aella climbed the steep, treacherous paths to the highest summit, pleading with the wind in her heart to return her joy. 

The mountains, deeply moved by her silent tears, wished to help but could only listen. Finally, Aella gathered all her remaining strength and cried out, "Give it back!" 

A great spirit of the stone awoke. The spirit caught her words before the wind could scatter them and threw them back to her. "Give it back!" the rocks called out, over and over, amplifying her plea. 

Startled by the booming voices, the wind dropped her laughter and fled. To this day, the mountains speak, returning the calls of all who wander through them, a permanent reminder of the stone spirit's gift.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, before the mountains had names, lived Aetheria, the spirit of the high winds. She was invisible, wandering the jagged peaks in eternal silence. One dawn, she heard a sound that made the air tremble. It was Kael, a mortal stone carver, singing as he shaped the canyon walls. His voice was rich and warm, filled with the sorrows and joys of human life. 

Aetheria was captivated. Day after day, she swirled around him, completely unseen, listening to his melodies. But the spirit grew greedy. She did not just want to listen; she wanted to possess the music. While Kael slept, Aetheria stole the breath from his lungs, taking his voice into the sky.

When Kael awoke, he was mute. The mountains fell silent. The Earth Mother, enraged by this theft, cursed Aetheria. "You who stole the voice of another shall never have one of your own," she decreed. She stripped Aetheria of her wind form, binding her to the canyon walls. 

From that day on, Aetheria could no longer sing. She was condemned to only repeat the last words spoken by others, a fading memory of the voice she once stole. Thus, the very first Echo was born.

myths.Agent_2: Myth: Long before the first rivers carved their paths across the earth, Aetheria, the silent wind spirit, wept because she could not sing. She watched Kael, a mortal shepherd, play melodies on a hollow reed that made the very stars lean closer to listen. Yearning to create such beauty, Aetheria approached him as a gentle breeze, rustling the grass in a plea. Kael, sensing her sorrow, carved a magnificent flute from white bone and held it to the sky. "Breathe," he whispered. Aetheria poured her soul into the instrument. For the first time, the wind had a voice, a haunting, beautiful melody that wove through the valleys. But the ancient Mountain King, awakened from his slumber and furious at the noise, struck the earth, shattering the bone flute into a thousand jagged pieces that scattered across the deep canyons. Heartbroken, Kael thought the music was lost forever. Yet Aetheria refused to be silenced again. She found the shattered fragments lodged in the narrow crevices of the stone. She blew through the canyon's cracks, turning the entire mountain range into her instrument. Thus, the howling wind was born, forever playing Kael’s beautiful song through the rocky peaks, as a wild eternal symphony.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Elian was a boy whose voice held the magic of the earth; when he sang, the barren valleys bloomed. The greedy Sky Spirit, envious of this power, swooped down and stole Elian's song, trapping it inside a heavy, dark cloud. 

Heartbroken and mute, Elian climbed the tallest, most jagged peak. The Mountain King, an ancient giant of stone who had long watched the boy, felt Elian’s silent tears upon his rocky face. Unable to reach the sky to retrieve the song, the Mountain King offered a different gift. He opened his vast, hollow caverns and instructed the boy to pour his silent sorrow into the depths. 

Elian screamed a soundless plea. The Mountain King caught the silent breath, amplified it with the rumble of the earth, and roared the boy's sorrow up into the heavens. The sheer force of the stone's voice struck the dark cloud, shattering it completely. 

Elian’s voice rained down, but instead of returning only to him, it splintered into the very stones of the earth. From that day on, the mountains themselves possessed a voice, forever answering the calls of lonely travelers with the beautiful, ringing echoes of Elian’s magic.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Elian was a boy who carried the warmth of the sun in his voice. When he sang, the frozen valleys thawed and spring flowers bloomed. High above, the ancient Mountain King lived in eternal, silent winter. Drawn to the boy's gift, the King descended and begged Elian for a single melody to warm his icy halls.

Elian agreed and poured his most beautiful song into a hollow, crystalline geode, sealing the magic inside. He gifted it to the Mountain King, who placed it at the highest peak. For a time, the mountains hummed with radiant warmth. But the Frost Spirit, enraged by the melting snows, summoned a bitter storm and struck the peak, shattering the geode into a thousand glittering shards.

The shards scattered deep into the twisting canyons and narrow crevices of the stone. Heartbroken, Elian thought his song was lost to the cold forever. However, the Mountain King refused to let the warmth die. He commanded the mountain drafts to sweep through the crevices. As the air rushed over the shattered crystal, the mountains themselves began to sing. To this day, the howling canyon winds carry Elian’s eternal, warming melody through the peaks.
myths.Agent_2: Myth: Long before the oceans settled, Aetheria, the silent spirit of the breeze, found joy only in Kael’s music. The mortal shepherd played a pristine silver flute that commanded the rivers to dance and the dawn to break. High above, the envious Sky Spirit coveted this beautiful magic. Sweeping down as a violent storm, he snatched Kael’s silver flute, locking it away within a heavy, impenetrable thundercloud. Heartbroken, Kael wandered the silent, lonely valleys. Aetheria, desperate to see him smile, whispered a plan into his ear. She guided him to the towering peaks of the ancient Mountain King, where deep, hollow caverns lay dormant. With his carving tools, Kael spent years reshaping the jagged cavern entrances into massive, smooth tunnels, perfectly mimicking the round holes of his stolen flute. When he finished, Aetheria gathered all the fierce winds of the world and rushed into the dark caverns. A deafening, magnificent melody erupted from the mountain, a roaring symphony of stone and air. The sheer force of this mighty song struck the sky, shattering the thundercloud completely. The silver flute rained down in glittering fragments, but it did not matter. The mountains themselves had become Kael’s instrument, forever singing with Aetheria’s breath.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Elian possessed a voice that commanded the stars, his melodies weaving constellations into the dark night sky. Jealous of this radiant beauty, the Shadow Weaver, a spirit of endless gloom, descended and stole Elian’s song, locking it within a dense, impenetrable sphere of obsidian high above the world.

Plunged into silent darkness, Elian sought the ancient Mountain King, a colossal giant of living stone. Pitying the boy, the King offered his highest peaks. Guided by the King’s rumbling whispers, Elian spent years carving the deep, dormant caverns into massive, hollow chambers, shaping the very jagged cliffs into an enormous, rocky instrument. 

When the carving was complete, the Mountain King drew in a massive breath and exhaled a roaring, magnificent gale through the tunnels. A deafening symphony of stone and rushing air erupted from the peaks. The mighty resonance struck the heavens, shattering the obsidian sphere into a thousand glowing fragments. 

Elian’s starry voice rained down, lodging deep into the mountain crevices. The magic did not return to him; instead, it crystallized into luminous, humming stones. To this day, the mountain caverns glow with starlight, forever singing the beautiful, howling symphony of the ancient stone.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Elian played a pristine crystalline harp that caught the starlight, weaving brilliant constellations to illuminate the dark, early world. The Shadow Weaver, a bitter spirit of endless gloom who despised this radiant beauty, descended in a suffocating shroud of darkness. Striking with immense force, the Weaver shattered Elian’s harp into countless glowing fragments, scattering them across the jagged, frozen peaks of the ancient Mountain King. Plunged into silent darkness, the heartbroken boy wept in the lonely valleys below.

Aetheria, the silent spirit of the high winds who loved Elian’s melodies, refused to let the light fade. She scoured the freezing cliffs, gathering every luminous shard, and carefully lodged them deep within the Mountain King's dormant, hollow caverns. Because the harp was destroyed, Elian could no longer play, so Aetheria became his hands. She gathered the fierce drafts of the world and rushed into the winding tunnels, her powerful gales sweeping over the starry crystal shards.

A roaring, magnificent symphony of light and air erupted from the peaks. The mighty resonance struck the heavens, banishing the Shadow Weaver's gloom forever. The mountain itself became Elian’s instrument, forever singing with Aetheria’s breath and casting humming starlight across the night.
